world_news.headline: Plague epidemic risk in Russia low after death of lab technician, WHO says
world_news.summary:
World Health Organization detects no sign of further outbreak since Darya Shipilova died last week

The World Health Organization has said the risk of an epidemic in Russia is low after the sudden death of a lab technician who worked at a plague research institute in Siberia.

Darya Shipilova, who was 28, died last week, two days after falling ill. Russian media reports suggested she may have become infected after an accident at her workplace, where dangerous pathogens are kept and studied.

world_news.headline: New Zealand greenhouse gas levels hit record highs threatening catastrophic glacier melts
world_news.summary:
Government report finds the country could be hit with more frequent and intense heatwaves, as well as damaging storms and cyclones

New Zealand could be hit with more frequent and intense heatwaves and catastrophic glacier melts in the near future, as greenhouse gas levels hit record highs, a new report about the nation’s climate has revealed.

Released on Wednesday, the Our Atmosphere and Climate 2026 report shows New Zealand is experiencing mounting climate pressures, which will have wide-reaching implications for the environment, native species and communities.

world_news.headline: Privacy watchdog launches probe into China-based company behind Kmart ‘pervert glasses’ app
world_news.summary:
Commissioner said Shenzhen Qingcheng, the app maker behind the HeyCyan app in the smartglasses, failed to respond to her inquiries

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian privacy regulator has opened an investigation into the China-based software company behind the HeyCyan app in Kmart’s $89 smartglasses, following public outrage over the covert use of the devices.

In August, Guardian Australia reported Kmart had sold out of the Anko-branded discount version of Meta’s smartglasses that can capture images and record high-definition video, which led to widespread concern and calls to ban or restrict their use.

world_news.headline: Ikea to pilot online buyback service for secondhand furniture
world_news.summary:
Service to be tested in Spain and Portugal this year, with a UK rollout if successful, as pre-loved markets boom

Ikea is to test an online version of its buy-back service where the retailer offers vouchers for unwanted secondhand furniture.

The service will be tested in Spain and Portugal before the end of December and will be launched in the UK if it proves successful. Ikea already offers buy-back in stores, including in the UK. The online version will extend it to a much wider audience, with Ikea predicting pre-owned goods are likely to grab 16% of the UK homewares market by next year

world_news.headline: Sarah Macdonald returns to ABC radio after being sacked in 2024
world_news.summary:
Manager who removed Macdonald announces she will replace the late James Valentine from March

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Two years after her shock axing the ABC has backflipped and reinstated ABC Radio presenter Sarah Macdonald to Sydney’s local radio schedule, where she will replace the late James Valentine from March.

The manager who had removed Macdonald without explanation, ABC director audio Ben Latimer, announced her return on Wednesday to take on the afternoons slot.
